note: A SEARCHED TEST FIXTURE PAYS ~4 s PER SEED AND CAN BECOME THE STRAGGLER THAT SETS A CRATES WHOLE WALL TIME. Measured in hornvale-vessel: one discriminator whose predicate first holds at seed 28 swept seeds 0..64 unordered, cost 136.5 s, and finished LAST of 582 tests with the crate at 201 s -- every other vessel test is under 7 s. Because it is a straggler, nextest parallelism cannot hide it; it sets the tail directly. Pinning the seed is the obvious fix and is WRONG here: windows/vessel/tests/common/mod.rs records that pinning this class of precondition rotted when the flagship was reseeded, which is why the search exists. A shallower BuildDepth is not available either -- a Session needs species and culture, so Full is the only rung. THE FIX IS TO ORDER THE SEARCH, NOT SHORTEN IT: a helper yielding once(hint).chain(RANGE.filter(!= hint)), where hint is the seed the fixture last hit on. The full range is still swept behind the hint, so a rotted hint costs one wasted build and the sweep still finds whichever seed satisfies the predicate; the loud panic at the end still fires only when nothing in the range works. The hint is a PERFORMANCE claim, never a correctness one, and nothing asserts on it. Result 136.5 s to 6.077 s, 22x. POSITIVE CONTROL MATTERS HERE because a faster green is exactly what a BROKEN search would also look like: mis-hint one fixture deliberately (via scripts/mutate.py, which refuses a substitution that is not found and unique) and confirm it still PASSES and merely gets slower -- ours went 8.135 s to 21.893 s, proving the sweep ran, skipped the bad hint and found the real seed. Restore from a /tmp copy, never git checkout --, which reverts the hints along with the mutation.
